clue.text: How much to turn bird to drink before a dress show?

parts.note: asking how much is asking the cost

indicators.note: to turn the bird is to write its name the other way round

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird
a dram is a small measure of spirits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling instruction about turning a bird to drink before attending a fashion show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses EMU to UME, so COST + UME gives the first word; DRAM + A gives the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A period drama on stage or screen is literally a show full of historical dresses, hence a dress show.

clue.text: Give up what sounds fruitful

indicators.note: what sounds like signals that the word suggested is heard rather than written

parts.note: seed is what fruit produces, so a fruitful word here is seed

explanation.surface: A riddle asking which word to surrender sounds productive.
explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish or surrender territory or a point is to give it up.

clue.text: Cannibalistic address to bird by Swinburne?

definitions.text: Cannibalistic address to bird by Swinburne?

parts.words: Cannibalistic address to bird by Swinburne?
parts.note: Read the bird name as a verb and the greeting becomes a call to eat one's own sibling

explanation.surface: A Victorian poet addressing a bird in apparently cannibalistic terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening line of Swinburne's Itylus is addressed to a swallow as a sister; taking 'swallow' as a command makes it cannibalistic.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the poet's apostrophe to a bird, which can also be read as an order to eat a sibling.

clue.text: Habits of high caste prophets

parts.note: U stands for upper class, the high caste of British society
sages are wise men, seers or prophets

explanation.surface: The customs of upper-caste seers.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' debate on British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Usages are customary practices, which are habits in the sense of established ways.

clue.text: No problem about consumption near Skipton

indicators.note: about places the disease abbreviation around the outside of the easy word

parts.note: no problem means easy
consumption is the old name for tuberculosis, TB

explanation.surface: Someone says tuberculosis is no problem, somewhere in Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Skipton is a market town in North Yorkshire; Eastby is a village close by.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a small Yorkshire village lying just outside Skipton, so it is a place near that town.

clue.text: See 19
Delusion suggesting cloned animal on public view?

parts.note: animals on public view are the zoo's
a cloned animal is a copy of the original

explanation.surface: A fantasy of a cloned beast exhibited to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as ZOO'S COPY: the zoo's cloned exhibit. The answer is a hallucination of seeing animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Zooscopy is a hallucinatory condition in which a person imagines seeing animals, a kind of delusion.

clue.text: Tile battered with rain, resisting change?

indicators.note: battered by rain, the letters of the two words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A roof tile beaten by rain yet standing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is the tendency of a body to resist a change in motion, so inertial describes that resistance.

clue.text: OM (Old Man) with old goal could be total misery

indicators.note: could be says these letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: An elderly man with an outdated ambition, told his lot is pure gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges OM, OLD MAN, OLD and GOAL, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a situation of complete pessimism and despair, which is total misery.

clue.text: Rules can change after row interrupts Rose Turner

indicators.note: interrupts places the following pieces into the middle of the other word
a turner turns things round, so the letters of the flower are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

indicators.note: after places the changed can behind the din

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the word can

parts.note: taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: Regulations governing a painter named Rose Turner after a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose Turner looks like a person's name; 'Turner' is an anagram signal turning the flower's letters to ORES, and 'change' turns the tin into ANC.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinances are authoritative decrees or regulations, which are rules.

clue.text: See 1
Most eggs, prepared for cooking outside, must be moved like coal

indicators.note: outside puts the cooking word around the trimmed eggs

parts.note: peas or eggs prepared for cooking are shelled

indicators.note: most of a word means drop its last letter

parts.note: ova are eggs

explanation.surface: Most of the eggs, readied for the pan, have to be shifted like coal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' drops the final letter of the eggs; 'outside' wraps the cooking word round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is traditionally moved with a shovel, so shovelled means moved in that manner.

clue.text: Shrub male god put in most of Channel Island

indicators.note: put in places the male and the god inside the trimmed island
most of drops the last letter of the island

parts.note: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands
a buck is a male deer or rabbit
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A male deity installed on a Channel Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Alderney is a Channel Island off Normandy; 'most of' drops its last two letters, and 'put in' sets the male and god inside before the final N.
explanation.definitionFit: Alder buckthorn is a small deciduous European shrub, Frangula alnus.

clue.text: Napper getting rude awakening if caught at it?

indicators.note: a rude awakening shakes up the sleeping napper, rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: A dozing person gets a rude shock when caught napping.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone caught in the act without warning is not ready, which is being unready.

clue.text: Amphibian, original model

parts.note: something original is new
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: An amphibian described as an original model.
explanation.definitionFit: The newt is a small tailed amphibian related to the salamander.

clue.text: Old soldier with oriental weapon in range

indicators.note: in places the eastern letter and the weapon inside the range

parts.note: a span is a range or extent
E for east, the oriental direction
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A veteran fighter bearing an Eastern weapon within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oriental weapon' looks like one item, but 'oriental' gives just E for east, and 'in' puts it with the weapon inside the range.
explanation.definitionFit: A spearman was a soldier armed with a spear, a figure of old armies.

clue.text: Vote for Reagan is very small

definitions.note: the definition describes the particle as being tiny

parts.note: to vote for someone is to elect them
Ron is short for Ronald, as in Ronald Reagan

explanation.surface: Voting for Reagan is a minor matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron is a subatomic particle, about as tiny as matter gets.

clue.text: Hat conceals gold from view

indicators.note: the hat conceals means the gold sits within it

parts.note: a Panama is a lightweight straw hat
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A hat hides gold from sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide unbroken view of a landscape.

clue.text: Where Charles got hiding after hiding out of Paddington?

definitions.text: Where Charles got hiding after hiding out of Paddington?

parts.words: Where Charles got hiding after hiding out of Paddington?
parts.note: Charles II escaped capture after the Battle of Worcester by hiding in a tree at Boscobel; a London tube station of the same name is the next stop out of Paddington

explanation.surface: A question about where King Charles concealed himself after leaving a London station.
explanation.walkthrough: Royalist legend says Charles II hid in an oak at Boscobel in 1651; the name also belongs to a pub chain and a station just west of Paddington.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree that hid the fleeing king shares its name with the station one stop out of Paddington.

clue.text: King by birth is bent

definitions.note: the definition describes the joint as something that bends

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
née means born, used before a maiden name

explanation.surface: A monarch by birth is crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the leg joint that is bent when walking or kneeling.

clue.text: Month before last at hour 4, in derogatory Latin 1across 9

indicators.note: in puts the run of short pieces within the slur

parts.note: dago is an offensive slang word for a Latin person, Italian or Spanish
Oct is short for October
or is an old word for before, as in 'or ever'
Z is the last letter of the alphabet
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Instructions about a month, an hour and a number, set inside some Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: OR as 'before' is archaic, as in Shakespeare's 'or ere'; 'in' puts all five pieces inside the slur, which is offensive and used here only as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: David Lean's film of Pasternak's novel is a sweeping historical costume drama.

clue.text: Ulster church officer gets on in nihilistic movement in 1across 9

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the art movement

parts.note: Dada was an anti-art movement rejecting all values
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
an elder is an officer of a Presbyterian church
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Ulster church official joins a nihilist art movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the Ulster abbreviation, the church officer and ON inside the doubled syllable of the art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot's last novel has been adapted for television as a period costume drama.

clue.text: Glorious revolutionary conferring with old ape in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A celebrated rebel consulting an elderly ape who is in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges CONFERRING, O and APE. The Glorious Revolution of 1688 brought William III to the English throne.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Orange was the leading figure of England's Glorious Revolution of 1688.

clue.text: Assist man with record

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man with a record offering assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To help someone is to assist them.

clue.text: Change art and end art — it will slow down

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Change art and end art — it will slow down' (9): ART AND gives six of the letters, but no reading of 'end art' supplies the remaining R, E, T, and no search found the original wording
annotationWithheld.clue: Change art and end art — it will slow down

clue.text: Proposer's words, saying he's got little time inside

indicators.note: inside places the short time within the contraction

parts.note: the man himself saying he has got would say I've
a mo is a moment, a little time

explanation.surface: A man proposing a motion says he has a moment to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: A proposer in a debate formally moves a motion; 'inside' puts the short time within the speaker's contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone proposing a motion formally opens with these words, moving it.

clue.text: See 20
List for cleaner joining her ring

parts.note: a roll is a list of names
a mop is a cleaning implement

explanation.surface: A list for a cleaning woman, joined to her ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Join HER and RING into one word: the answer is a pickled fillet of that fish rolled up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a rolled, pickled fillet of the fish formed by joining the clue's two words.
